AGENDA
  MEETING OF THE GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  JUNE 03, 2019
  4:00 PM

  1. ROLL CALL

  2. CONSENT ITEMS
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by
  making such request before motion is proposed.

  a. Approval of the minutes for the May 6, 2019 Meeting

  3. GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

  4. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Legislative Update
  b. Budget Presentation
  c. Strategic Plan

  5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes
  Discussion is limited to items NOT part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5) minutes – Commission may question or respond to the speaker, but there
  will be no debate or decision. The General Manager may refer the matter to appropriate staff for investigation and report.

  6. AGENDA FORECAST

  7. ADJOURNMENT

  Next Meeting is scheduled for July 1, 2019

Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water & Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for
program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling (818) 548-2090. Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp. PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the GWP Administration Office 141 N.
Glendale Avenue 4th Floor, Glendale, CA 91206. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact Catalina Lee (818) 548-2107 during regular
business hours.
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  MEETING OF THE GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  June 3, 2019
  4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  Present: President Avanessian, Commissioners Carrasco, Kedikian, Lall and Watson

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the May 6, 2019 Meeting Minutes
  Motion to Approve:
  Moved by: Commissioner Lall
  Seconded by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Motion Passed.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioners Lall and Watson commended staff on the June 1, 2019 Tail Gate event. The Commissioners
  commented that it was informative, engaging, and fun. Commissioner Carrasco praised GWP crews for recent work in
  the Adams Hill. He commented that the outreach and notification was excellent and traffic impacts were minimal for a
  large project in an area with limited parking.

4. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Legislative Update. Leo Zalyan, GWP Administrative Analyst, presented key energy and water bills. On the
  electric side, Mr. Zalyan covered the Governor’s declaration of a Wildfire State of Emergency and wildfire legislation, SB
  772 (bulk storage), AB 288 (self-generation bill of rights); AB 1208 (utility user’s tax exemption for clean energy), and
  AB 1799 (natural gas price volatility). On the water side, Mr. Zalyan mentioned the Governor’s executive order on water
  resiliency; the California WaterFix; AB 217 (water tax); SB 414 (small system water authority), SB 669 (safe drinking
  water fund); SB 134 (water loss performance standards); AB 1180 (recycled water); AB 60 (water meters); AB 1414
  (urban retail water suppliers reporting); and SB 1 (California Environmental Public Health and Workers Defense Act of
  2019). He responded to the Commissioner’s questions regarding specific legislative items.

  In response to question from Commissioner Watson, Mr. Zurn explained that GWP’s procedure with regard to
  legislation is to work with numerous utility organizations and lobbyists to track and analyze legislation, and any
  statements or positions on behalf of the City are approved by the mayor, and if the GWP Commission has any
  recommendations, those can be passed along.

  b. Budget Presentation. Alina Morshidian, GWP Utility Manager, presented GWP’s Fiscal Year 2019-20 proposed
  budget, including departmental dashboards, a summary of the budget by fund, and the capital improvement programs
  for electric and water. Ms. Morshidian and Mr. Zurn explained the reasoning for the line items with larger percentage
  increases compared to previous years, such as the increase in the electric depreciation fund covers added gas and
  power purchase costs due to the loss of the use of the Scholl landfill gas at Grayson, opportunities to buy additional
  green energy, and the need to ensure supplies for the summer. Mr. Zurn stated that the increase in the electric
   customer capital fund covers pole replacement, wildfire mitigation, and infrastructure programs from the Cost of Service
  Analysis (COSA). Mr. Zurn stated that the increase in the water depreciation fund covers water capital items in line with
  GWP’s master plan. Staff responded to Commissioners’ questions regarding the OSISoft Pi Historian Enterprise, water
  and electric landscaping and security upgrades at GWP facilities; the backup power program; the water quality
  enhancement program; pipeline replacements and detection of pipe corrosion, and utility reserves. In response to a
  question from Commissioner Lall, Mr. Zurn responded that GWP is in a very good position financially, and has the
  budget, but not necessarily the time, to implement the projects it wants to implement.

  c. Strategic Plan. Mr. Craig Kuennen, Business Transformation and Marking Administrator, presented GWP’s vision,
  mission, core values, and the six strategic focus areas of GWP’s Strategic Plan, namely: Affordability and Fiscal
  Responsibility, Exceptional Customer Service, Workforce, Reliability, Sustainability, and Automation and Innovation.
  Commissioner Watson commended GWP on an aggressive and comprehensive plan, and inquired if the plan was or
  would be approved by the City Council. Mr. Zurn responded that the plan does not require City Council approval, but
  will be presented periodically to the GWP Commission. In response to a question from Commissioner Lall, staff
  responded that GWP does not have electric vehicle installations planned at Glendale Community College but is open to
  working with them. Commissioner Carrasco suggested adding “affordability” to GWP’s mission and vision statement
  and suggested that GWP consider partnering with the school district to identify customers that may be eligible for the
  Care Program. Commissioner Carrasco inquired whether GWP benchmarks against other utilities, and Mr. Zurn
  responded that GWP does do so in a number of areas, and could include some benchmarking information in future
  reports to the Commission on the Strategic Plan. With regard to the Workforce focus area, Commissioner Carrasco
  asked if GWP has a knowledge transfer program, and Mr. Zurn affirmed that succession planning, including retaining
  newly-trained and hired employees, is an ongoing and important exercise.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  President Avanessian and Commissioners Watson and Kedikian confirmed attendance for a July 1, 2019 meeting
  regarding the Clean Energy Request for Proposals.

  President Avanessian inquired about a presentation regarding transmission. Mr. Zurn confirmed that he is planning to
  bring such a report to the Commission in the future, and will look at scheduling a meeting focused on transmission for
  September. Commissioner Carrasco requested that the presentation regarding transmission include a discussion
  regarding wildfire mitigation.

  President Avanessian inquired about a presentation on Utility Modernization. Mr. Zurn responded that Mr. Kuennen
  periodically presents reports on utility modernization efforts to the Commission, the most recent of which covered
  electric vehicles, and he will continue to do so.

7. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Watson
  Seconded by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 5:20 pm.
